newsitem.title: USA: SouthTrust official says company not for sale.
newsitem.headline: SouthTrust official says company not for sale.

text.p: SouthTrust Corp's investor relations director adamantly insisted Wednesday that the banking company is no candidate for a merger despite Wall Street's long held speculation to the contrary.
"There is no for sale sign up," the executive, C.H. "Butch" Crouch said in answer to a question from the floor after he addressed the Atlanta Society of Financial Analysts.
"The odds of us selling the bank are about nil," said Crouch, the company's senior vice president for investor relations.
Wall Street analysts, however, have speculated for a decade that the medium-sized Birmingham, Ala.-based bank holding company is an ideal candidate to be acquired by a larger institution.

Analysts say the $26.2-billion asset company is too large to compete against fleet-footed smaller banks and yet not large enough to offer the services and lending capacities of money center and super-regional banks. SouthTrust executives consistently maintain they have developed strategies to overcome those perceived shortcomings.

Crouch said SouthTrust management has never even hinted that it would welcome a merger as have other peer group institutions as a means to help bolster the price of their common stock. "We don't even flirt," he said. "Some other banks say, 'We're for sale, but maybe not.'"

Another SouthTrust executive, Thomas Coley, chairman and chief executive of the company's Georgia operation, SouthTrust Bank of Georgia, told the analysts, "If you're buying our stock, buy it on performance. Don't buy it on takeover (speculation)."

Separately, Crouch described in an interview as "reasonable" Wall Street's consensus earnings per share estimate for 1997 of $3 versus $2.69 in 1996. During his presentation to analysts, Crouch said that the company's five-year goal beginning in 1997 is to achieve an annual return on equity rate of 18 percent, compared with 16 percent during the previous five years.
